summary: Builds the capture checklist text via buildCapturePayload({root,cli,sid,entries,envelope}). The envelope selects the opening line and tail: 'block' (handle capture now, then stop), 'subagent' (adds the restate-your-deliverable tail, because the coordinator sees only the sub's last message), 'manual' (#84 - names the user's own /capture-notes invocation) and anything else falls through to the non-blocking 'handle capture first, then continue'. A .coldstart/checklist.md override replaces the shipped body wholesale, substituting {{WORKLIST}}/{{CLI}}/{{ROOT}}/{{SID}}, and the worklist is auto-appended if the override omits its placeholder.

summary: Builds the v5 capture checklist delivered at Stop/SubagentStop. CHANGED 2026-07-30 (PR #114): rule 7 was the root cause of alias bloat — it asked for SYMPTOM WORDS with no length or quality bound, so agents wrote symptom sentences and every content word inside became an independent match chance (one note reached 34 aliases / 108 name tokens and won 27% of all injections). It now says aliases are search keys: 2-5 words each, no filler, covering the vocabulary the file itself owns, 6-10 total. The motivating instance: this file owns the alias rule, had 18 aliases, and not one contained the word 'aliases' — so a prompt asking about aliases could not surface it. NOTE the blast radius: the rule only shapes notes captured AFTER the change; existing notes keep their aliases until re-written.

summary: Builds the capture prompt (v5) delivered by the elicit hooks. Three changes 2026-07-31, each fixing an observed capture failure rather than a style preference. (1) The flow spec is now INLINE next to the file-note shapes instead of deferred to 'run kb write with no spec to print the guide' — that bounce was the cause of stepless flows: agents write from memory rather than bouncing, and memory holds the file-note shape (title + summary), which folds to a note with zero anchors. Any shape that must be right on the first try belongs in the prompt, not behind a bounce. (2) Rule 3a pushes back on UNDER-capture. The prompt carried three brakes (present-code-only, no-note-is-fine, the partial-read warning) and no counterweight, and a real session surfaced 30+ worked files and produced 8 notes; 3a makes a note the default for an [edited] file, asks for an explicit decision per worklist row, and requires naming the files skipped so a silent skip becomes a stated one. (3) The FLOW DECISION section now rides on the last kb write via --decision instead of being a mandatory second command. The worklist is still the scope rule and is load-bearing — a checklist override that omits {{WORKLIST}} gets it appended anyway.

summary: Builds the capture prompt (v5) delivered by the elicit hooks, and — as of 2026-08-01 — is also the single choke point where the session WORKLIST MANIFEST is recorded. Every host (Claude, Cursor, Codex) calls buildCapturePayload with {root, cli, sid, entries}, so recordWorklistManifest() writes tmpdir/coldstart-kb-worklist-<sid>.json there: one entry per worklist file with its tier and a needsNote flag (no note, or a stale one). That file is the DENOMINATOR for capture coverage — `kb write --session` reads it back and prints 'N of M worklist files noted'. It is a deliberate side effect in an otherwise pure prompt builder, wrapped in try/catch because capture must never fail for it; its contract twin is src/kb/session-worklist.ts and the filename must stay in step with that file. Earlier 2026-07-31 changes still hold: the flow spec is INLINE next to the file-note shapes (the 'run kb write with no spec' bounce was the cause of stepless flows — agents write from memory, and memory holds the file-note shape), rule 3a makes a note the DEFAULT for an [edited] file and now also tells the agent to read the coverage line back, and FLOW DECISION rides on the last kb write via --decision.

summary: Builds the capture prompt (v5) for every host, and is the single choke point where the session worklist manifest is written (recordWorklistManifest -> tmpdir/coldstart-kb-worklist-<sid>.json, the DENOMINATOR kb write reads back for its coverage line; contract twin src/kb/session-worklist.ts). THE HAZARD THIS FILE OWNS: it INLINES its own copy of the kb write spec shapes, deliberately (the 'run kb write with no spec' bounce was what produced stepless flows — agents write from memory rather than bouncing). Two hand-maintained copies drift, and did: the inlined flow shape lost "aliases", and every flow written from it landed in the notebook reachable only by its exact title. tests/kb-shape-parity.test.ts now pins this copy to WRITE_GUIDE_SHAPES field-for-field — if you edit a shape here, that test is what tells you the other copy moved. Both shapes now carry aliases AND symbols. Rule 3a (a note is the DEFAULT for an [edited] file, skips must be named) and the flow-decision-rides-on-kb-write flag are also here; the worklist is the scope rule and a checklist override that omits {{WORKLIST}} gets it appended anyway.

summary: Builds the capture prompt (v5) for every host. 2026-08-06: the static DECIDE-FIRST/per-note/FLOWS/WRITE instructions (~150 lines, byte-identical every fire) no longer get duplicated onto disk per session. shippedInstructionsTemplate() is written ONCE to the permanent, gitignored `.coldstart/notebook/.capture-instructions.md` (ensureCaptureInstructions — version-tagged via INSTRUCTIONS_VERSION so a future template change self-heals a stale on-disk copy instead of drifting silently). renderCapturePayload substitutes {{CLI}}/{{ROOT}}/{{SID}}/{{AID}}/{{WORKLIST}} into that permanent body — the SAME placeholder mechanism the pre-existing `.coldstart/checklist.md` user-override path already used (loadChecklistOverride now takes precedence, ensureCaptureInstructions is the fallback; both paths share one substitution pass now instead of two near-duplicate branches). The per-session `.worklist-<sid>-<aid>.md` (writeDurableWorklist/renderDurableMd) is now SMALL — just the worklist + a pointer to the permanent file — instead of the full rendered payload. Nothing changes for the CURRENT fire: buildCapturePayload's return value (what the agent actually reads this turn) still inlines the complete instructions text every time; only what gets persisted to disk for a LATER re-Read shrank (~10KB -> ~400 bytes per session). This does not touch the worklist-deletion recovery fix from the same week (see the flow note) — that's about the JSON half (files/tier/needsNote), which must stay per-session and deletable; this split only concerns the static prose half.
